questions.prompt: Two mounted servers, `tracker` and `wiki`, both offer a tool named `search`. What does the model see?
options: One `search` tool, and the client picks a server at random
An error, because names must be unique across servers
questions.explanation: Each tool is registered with a server prefix, so equal names from different servers stay distinct and show where a call goes.

questions.prompt: Your sandbox runs in workspace-write. Does it stop an MCP server you started from writing to your home folder?
options: No; the fence wraps commands your shell tool runs, not a server program you started yourself
Yes; every child program of the harness is fenced automatically
Yes, because MCP servers can only read files
Only if the server's tools are approved first
questions.explanation: The fence applies to commands the shell tool confines. A server is its own program with your permissions, so adding one is a trust decision.

questions.prompt: A server answers a call with isError: true. What does the mounted tool do?
options: Returns the text as a normal result
Retries the call until it succeeds
Throws, so the tool pipeline turns it into a tool error result for the model
questions.explanation: Throwing lets the existing pipeline mark the result as an error, so the model can read what went wrong and recover, as with any tool.
